quotes.text: organisations have had enough time to move beyond the emergency experiment of the pandemic
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: We know now what the challenges are,
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: We’ve had enough time to recognise that work intensification and socialisation are probably the two primary challenges.
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: For hybrid workers and fully remote workers, it’s about the fact that you can return to work so easily,
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: Those barriers stopping you from returning to work or keeping working are no longer there.
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: a blanket legal response risks cutting across the autonomy that makes hybrid work attractive
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: For some people, they want to be able to send their emails at night. That’s what the flexibility is offering them,
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: It’s about organisational culture. Yes, you can send your emails at this time of night, but don’t have any expectations of replies.
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: It should be productivity, not presenteeism,
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: You should be measured by what you produced rather than how many hours you were sitting at your desk.
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: What is the point of having an anchor day where you’re still having hybrid meetings, or you’re sitting there staring at your computer? Make sure when people do come in that it’s worth their while,
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: We’ve taken away the commute. We’ve taken away that natural end of the workday,
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: So you need to do it for yourself.
quotes.speaker: e1

quotes.text: But there were certainly those who said it’s good – but it could be better.
quotes.speaker: e1
